History of Present Illness:
___ M with alcoholic cirrhosis and active ETOH abuse who 
presents with increased abdominal pain x 4d. 
.
Patient was admitted for similar but more severe symptoms 3 
months ago at ___. At that time, pt had EGD only positive for 
gastritis and was started on omeprazole, with good improvement 
temporarily. Patient reports that after this hospitalization, he 
began drinking again, approximately 1 pint per day, and over the 
last week has been drinking 2 pints per day. His pain returned 4 
days ago, diffuse across the upper abdomen, occasionally sharp 
but not radiating, most tender in the mid-epigastrum. Not 
associated with fever. He reports decreased POs over the last 2 
days, only able to drink some water and ginger ale. He reports 
vomiting when he did try to take POs. No blood in emesis. No 
diarrhea, no blood in stool. Pt initially presented to ___ 
where US c/f cholecystitis vs CBD stone, given 2gm IV Unasyn and 
was transferred to ___ for possible ERCP.  
.  
In the ED, initial VS were: 98.3 75 132/70 16 95. Exam notable 
for diffuse pain to deep palpatin of abdomen. RUQ US: No 
cholelithiasis or cholecystitis, Echogenic liver (fatty or 
cirrhosis). On exam icteric, RUQ tender. Labs: Tbili 3.7 
(hemolyzed), alk phos 207, INR 1.4. He was given dilaudid, 
valium (although not scoring on CIWA x 3, had scored 12 and 4 at 
___), 2L IVF. Given no fever or WBC, unremarkable US, patient 
admitted for hepatitis workup. No plan for ERCP.  
.  
Vitals on transfer were 97.8 126/72 HR 71 RR 18 97% RA. On 
arrival to the floor patient reports that he feels that he is 
withdrawing and abdominal pain persists. This morning his 
abdominal pain is improved, but still ___, diffuse across the 
upper abdomen. He does have an appetitite and would like to eat. 
He states that he is having pins and needles in his fingers and 
anxiety, which he says are signs of withdrawl for him. He is 
interested in detox.   
.

Denied nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation. No recent

REASON FOR EXAM: Right upper quadrant pain. Clinical concern for 
cholecystitis. 
COMPARISON: None. 
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND: Liver is echogenic with 
enlargement of 
caudate lobe and nodular contour . There is no intrahepatic 
biliary ductal 
dilatation. Common bile duct measures about 4 mm. Portal vein 
demonstrates 
reversal of flow but appears patent. There is no gallbladder 
wall thickening with no evidence of gallstones or sonographic 
___ sign. The gallbladder is not significantly distended. 
Pancreatic head and neck appear unremarkable. Pancreatic body 
and tail are obscured by overlying bowel gas. 
IMPRESSION: 
1. Diffuse liver disease with possible cirrhosis. Reversed 
portal vein flow compatible with portal hypertension.  
2. No evidence of cholelithiasis or cholecystitis. No 
intrahepatic or 
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  
 
Brief Hospital Course:
*PATIENT LEFT THE HOSPITAL AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE*
.
Mr. ___ was admitted to the hospital with abdominal 
pain. RUQ ultrasound was negative for gallstones. His pain was 
most likely caused by known gastritis exacerbated by increased 
alcohol use. He was treated with pantoprazole and his pain was 
managed. His pain resolved and he was able to tolerate a regular 
diet. He will be discharged on his prior home dose of 
omeprazole. All other home medications were continued.   
.
Patient was monitored with CIWA scale for alcohol withdrawal. He 
experienced withdrawal symptoms and was treated with diazepam 
IV. Patient expressed desire to leave the hospital, despite his 
withdrawal symptoms, against medical advice. Psychiatry was 
consulted. Psychiatry believed he had capacity to make medical 
decisions and recommended diazepam PO taper on the following 
schedule:
.
Day 1 (___): 10 mg valium three times daily (total 30 mg 
daily)
Day 2 (___): 10 mg valium twice daily, 5 mg valium daily 
(total 25 mg daily) 
Day 3 (___): 10 mg valium twice daily (total 20 mg daily)
Day 4 (___): 10 mg valium daily, 5 mg valium daily (total 
15 mg daily) 
Day 5 (___): 10 mg valium once daily or 5 mg twice daily 
(total 10 mg daily) 
Day 6 (___): 5 mg valium once daily (total 5 mg daily) 
.
Patient was given folic acid, thiamine, and multivitamins during 
his hospitalization. He was discharged with a prescription for a 
total of three days of thiamine and maintenance multivitamins.   

.
Patient demonstrated understanding of the risks of leaving the 
hospital against medical advice. Patient has been instructed to 
schedule a follow-up appointment with his primary care 
physician. He has also been told to follow-up with his 
outpatient detoxification program.

Home

Gastritis
Alcohol withdrawal

 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.

 
Discharge Instructions:
You have decided to leave the hospital against medical advice. 
It has been explained to you that you are in alcohol withdrawal, 
which may worsen when you leave. Alcohol withdrawal puts you at 
risk for serious medical complications including seizures and 
death. We believe that you should stay in the hospital for 
monitoring and treatment of your withdrawal. Psychiatry has 
evaluated you and decided that you have the capacity to decide 
to leave against our advice.
. 
You were admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain. An 
ultrasound of your liver and gallbladder was performed, which 
did not show problems with your gallbladder. It is most likely 
that your pain was caused by your gastritis, which was 
exacerbated by alcohol use. You were given medications for 
gastritis and pain. Your pain resolved and you were able to eat 
a regular diet. You should restart your home omeprazole for 
treatment of your gastritis.
.
You experienced symptoms of alcohol withdrawal and received 
medication for this. You wanted to leave the hospital against 
medical advice, and psychiatry was called to evaluate you. They 
determined that you had capacity to decide to leave and gave 
recommendations regarding valium (diazepam) taper. You will be 
discharged to home on valium for your symptoms of withdrawal on 
the following schedule:
.
Day 1 (___): 10 mg valium three times daily (total 30 mg 
this day)
Day 2 (___): 10 mg valium in the morning and evening, 5 mg 
valium in the afternoon (total 25 mg this day) 
Day 3 (___): 10 mg valium twice daily (total 20 mg this 
day)
Day 4 (___): 10 mg valium in the morning, 5 mg valium in 
the evening (total 15 mg this day) 
Day 5 (___): 10 mg valium once (total 10 mg this day) 
Day 6 (___): 5 mg valium once (total 5 mg this day) 
.
Please do not take this medication if you are feeling sleepy or 
confused. Do not drive or operate machinery while taking this 
medication.
.
Please schedule a follow-up appointment with your primary care 
provider for later this week. Please also continue to attend 
your outpatient detoxification program.
